To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed the first sandwich "cavity-hexaphyrin-cavity" hybrid that behaves as a dual-responsive double-latch switch.
the first hexaphyrin-based sandwich hybrid has been designed and synthesized, and that its structure, conformation, and reactivity have been investigated.

we have developed a new class of hybrid systems based on a central hexaphyrin device that switches its conformation and oxidation state reversibly and independently under thermal and redox control, respectively, and that this device can be locked or unlocked by the two orthogonal switches depending on the oxidation state and conformation of the central device.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and the characterization of new compounds with interesting properties.
the design and synthesis of new molecules and supramolecular systems, and their applications in the field of catalysis.
the synthesis of novel molecular architectures based on the combination of cyclodextrins, hexaphyrins and porphycenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed an unprecedented dual-responsive "latched" device that is able to reversibly lock and unlock two communicating cavities by two independent orthogonal switches.
this work represents the first example of a sandwiched cavity-catalyst-cavities system with a hexaphyrinic central device.

the present work is an excellent contribution to the development of new hybrid materials, which are of high interest in the fields of molecular recognition, molecular catalysis and molecular machines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new strategy for designing a dual responsive double-latched device, which can serve as a model for allosteric enzyme mimic.
we have developed a new class of hybrid systems that are responsive to both temperature and redox stimuli.

we have developed a novel type of sandwich hybrids made of cyclodextrins linked on each side to a redox- and thermally switchable hexaphyrin and that the latter displays four interconvertible states under control of orthogonal switches, which are reversibly connected by the oxidation state of the central heteroannulenic macrocycle and the shape of the latter.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of hexaphyrin as a central device in sandwiched hybrids is a powerful strategy to achieve dual control of a confined space, and this approach could be extended to other macrocycles, such as calixarenes or cucurbiturils, to develop more sophisticated systems with multiple switches.
a hexaphyrinic central device is able to switch the communication between the two cyclodextrin cavities, thus leading to a dual-responsive double-latching system.
we developed a new class of hybrid molecules made of two cyclodeoxyribose rings triply linked to a hexaphyrins.
